points.description: States that a pointer is an address (a memory address) — i.e. it holds/stores/is the address of something, using the term 'address'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it says it 'refers to' or 'points to' a variable or value but does not use the term address precisely.

points.description: States that the address is of a location in memory (a memory location, e.g. of a variable), using the terms 'location' and 'memory'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only 'memory' or only 'location' is mentioned without the full phrase.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes the pointer (an address/variable holding an address) from the value stored at that location, i.e. does not describe a pointer as the data/value itself.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact: a pointer is an address of a location in memory, with the terms 'address' and 'memory location' used. Vague statements such as 'it points to something' or 'it refers to a variable' earn little or nothing; any wrong statement (e.g. a pointer is a value or a data type holding data) loses the affected point. Extra correct detail is allowed.
